issues.issue: The clause carves out liability for manufacture "occurring before PRI's receipt of such notice" and then adds that PRI "shall have no liability by reason of such manufacture at any time", which negates the whole undertaking. The two limbs of the same sentence contradict each other.

The "continuing right at all times" to manufacture and sell recompilation Albums is made subject only to paragraph 5.01(b)(ix)(B), and so appears to override the three-Album "Greatest Hits" ceiling in paragraph 5.01(b)(ix)(A). Whether the ceiling survives this provision is genuinely open.

This suspension rule excludes October, November and December while the parallel rule closing paragraph 5.01(c) excludes only November and December. The unexplained divergence between two adjacent computation rules invites argument that one is a slip.

The sentence covers "each of the first Albums ... and ... each of the second Albums ..." but then attaches a single "but only if" sales/chart condition, leaving it unclear whether the condition qualifies the second Albums alone or both. Whether PRI owes a Video for a first Album turns on that reading.

Concert Video terms are to be "negotiated in good faith" while "neither party shall be deemed obligated to reach any such agreement or to grant its consent" — an agreement to agree that gives a court nothing to enforce. The content of the good-faith duty is left undefined.

The power of attorney is triggered where Grantor "unreasonably refuses to do so and/or fails to return the same to PRI within ten (10) days"; the "and/or" leaves it unclear whether mere lateness, without unreasonableness, suffices. The scope of PRI's self-help right turns on that connector.

This paragraph grants PRI a perpetual right to use Artist's name and likeness "in connection with other merchandising of any kind", while paragraph 5.04(c) has Grantor "expressly reserve[] the right to exploit Artist's name, likenesses and biographies in all forms of merchandising". The two grants cover the same subject matter in opposite directions.

Likenesses supplied by Grantor are "deemed approved by Grantor" until notice, yet the final sentence excuses "any inadvertent failure by PRI to obtain the aforesaid approval" from being a breach, hollowing out the approval right. What remedy Grantor has for an unapproved use is unclear.

Grantor's reservation of "all forms of merchandising" cannot be squared with paragraph 5.04(a), which grants PRI a perpetual right to use the same names and likenesses "in connection with other merchandising of any kind". Which party may exploit merchandising rights is left genuinely contradictory.

The identity of Grantor's "current arrangement" counterparty is illegible/blank in the executed text, and the condition "provided PRI at the time has in the past and can arrange a 'first-class' merchandising activity" is ungrammatical and unmeasurable. Whether the Matching Right ever attaches cannot be determined from the words.

Advances are payable in instalments "promptly following" notice of commencement of recording, of mixing and of delivery, with no definition of "promptly" and no outside date. Timeliness of each instalment is left to construction.

Grantor is made responsible for "all Recording Costs", yet paragraph 3.02 requires PRI to approve the recording budget and to schedule and book studio time, and paragraph 6.01(b) fixes Advances by reference to that budget. Where responsibility for costs incurred under a PRI-controlled booking falls is not resolved.

The 10%-per-month reduction runs from "the last date such Album would otherwise be timely delivered pursuant to paragraph 4.01", but paragraph 4.01(d)(i) provides that delivery within sixty days of the stated date is not a failure to comply. Whether the Final Date includes that sixty-day grace is a genuine conflict.

The first sentence conditions Advance treatment of payments made on Grantor's behalf on PRI "obtain[ing] Grantor's prior approval", and the second says PRI "shall not be obligated to consult with Grantor" before making such payments, which are switched terms (approval versus consultation). The two sentences do not fit together.

Cross-collateralisation with the Polydor Agreements interacts with the Article 7 preamble, under which no royalties are payable "until such time as all Advances ... have been repaid"; whether Polydor advances count toward that condition is not stated. The two provisions leave the recoupment pool undefined.

Half of the $160,000 tour support is declared "non-returnable, non-recoupable" and "not Advances", but the provision says nothing about the status of the other half. The silence leaves the treatment of the balance open.

The preamble says no royalties accrue or are payable until all Advances "have been repaid to PRI", language of repayment rather than recoupment from royalties, which is circular if royalties cannot accrue until the Advances are repaid. The parenthetical "(except for accounting purposes)" does not resolve the circularity.

Paragraph 8.01 requires PRI to pay accrued royalties semi-annually "less Advances or other recoupable amounts hereunder", which assumes royalties accrue and are netted, contrary to this preamble's bar on any accrual until Advances are repaid. The two accounting mechanics differ.

The 11% rate applies to "Net Sales of all Albums sold by PRI for distribution through Normal Retail Channels in the United States"; whether a given exploitation (in particular new digital configurations) is an Album "sold" through "Normal Retail Channels" or is instead a licensed use is genuinely open on these words. The whole royalty owed turns on that characterisation.

This rate cannot be reconciled with paragraph 7.06(a), which fixes 50% of PRI's net receipts for licences of Master Recordings; a single exploitation can plausibly be described as both an Album sold through Normal Retail Channels and a licence, and the agreement gives no priority rule. Which paragraph governs is the core construction question.

"In excess of one hundred thousand (100,000) units" does not say whether the escalated 12% applies only to units above the threshold or retroactively to all units. That is a recurring escalation ambiguity.

As with 7.02(b), "in excess of two hundred fifty thousand (250,000) units" leaves open whether the 13% rate applies only to the excess units or to all units once the threshold is passed. The computation of royalties turns on that reading.

The flat 14% Japan rate sits alongside paragraph 6.04(a), which cross-collateralises this agreement with the Polydor K.K. (Japanese) recording agreements, leaving it unclear which instrument governs royalties on Japanese sales. That overlap is not addressed anywhere.

This list names Sweden and Denmark individually, while paragraph 5.01(d) uses the undefined collective "Scandinavia" for the same region; the instrument treats the territory inconsistently. Which countries belong where is left unresolved.
